evidence: Subdividing every K3,3 edge once gives a 15-vertex, 18-edge graph of genus 4 with the three midpoint chips vertex-supported.

For D0-a0, a fresh Dhar burn from a0 burns all 15 vertices; the three chip-bearing midpoints burn once they have two burned neighbors. Thus D0-a0 is a0-reduced with coefficient -1 at a0 and is not equivalent to an effective divisor.
Because D0 itself is effective, r(D0)>=0, while the single point a0 witnesses r(D0)<1; hence r(D0)=0.
The graph-to-metric rank equality theorem applies to the subdivided model; uniform rescaling from subdivided unit lengths to original unit K3,3 lengths preserves divisor rank.
The current main-branch record tree equals the assigned tree SHA.
correctness.summary: The matching-midpoint divisor on the unit K3,3 metric graph has Baker-Norine rank exactly zero.

originality.summary: General K3,3 gonality and graph/metric rank literature does not determine this specific matching-midpoint divisor. Targeted searches did not locate the named divisor or its rank, supporting originality of the exact cell computation but not an exhaustive novelty claim.

scientific_value.summary: The rank-zero certificate directly refutes the proposed rank-one lifting-gap witness and prevents downstream non-liftability work from being built on a false premise. It is also a reusable exact divisor-class datum.

limitations: The result concerns the named matching-midpoint divisor only; other degree-3 divisors on K3,3 may have rank one.
No lifting or non-lifting conclusion is made once the rank-one premise fails.
